name: Chile
summary_text: Chile has a strong legal framework — a gender identity law allowing self-determination (2019, no medical requirements), marriage equality (2022), a hate-crime law covering gender identity (2012), and a positive Gendarmería protocol that places trans inmates in facilities matching their gender identity and provides healthcare examination (better than most European countries on axis-H). The UN Human Rights Committee commended Chile's police measures to promote LGBTIQ rights. But 2024 was a "year of regression" (the first rollback since democracy returned in 1990), with lawmakers rejecting nondiscrimination-law reforms and a 2025 Movilh report describing a "breakdown of social, political and institutional consensus" on LGBTIQ+ rights. Documented violence includes a trans person murdered and dismembered ("the biggest hate crime in Chile"), a transphobic hotel attack in Santiago (beating, captivity, death threats), and institutional discrimination against Chile's first trans police officer. The Supreme Court restored a femicide conviction for the murder of a trans woman (overturning an appeals-court ruling that she didn't "legally qualify" as a woman). For a visitor: no border friction, bathrooms unrestricted, Santiago is welcoming.

sources.title: Chile | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex marriage and adoption legal since March 2022; hate-crime law includes SOGI as aggravating circumstances since 2012; civil unions since 2015; comprehensive self-determination-based legal gender recognition law passed 2019; third sex option for intersex children on birth certificates since 2006; non-binding intersex-affirming health guidance (2023) recommends against unnecessary surgeries; in 2025 a court issued Chile's first lesbophobic femicide conviction.

sources.title: 2024 was ‘year of regression’ for LGBTQ rights in Chile
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Mar 2025): '2024 was a 'year of regression' for LGBTQ rights in Chile' — annual rights report finds setbacks for equality and trans rights, including stalled legislation.
NOTE: The MOVILH (Chilean LGBT integration movement) 24th Annual Human Rights Report on sexual and gender diversity (2025) returned no extractable text at fetch time (image-based PDF).

sources.title: Descuartizado y ocultado por 24 horas: Ever, la víctima del "crimen de odio más grande de Chile" | bbcl_investiga | BioBioChile
sources.claim_summary: BioBioChile investigation (Jan 2024, in Spanish): profile of Ever, a young trans man murdered and dismembered in 2023 - described as Chile's 'biggest hate crime'; the killer, an acquaintance, confessed.

sources.title: “Me decía que me quería matar”: El crudo relato de una de las víctimas del ataque transfóbico en hotel de Santiago
sources.claim_summary: Chilevisión (Sept 2021, in Spanish): a 20-year-old trans man and his girlfriend were beaten with bottles and clubs and held against their will for nearly an hour at a Santiago hotel in a transphobic attack; victim recounts fearing for his life.

sources.title: “Que puedan manifestar el género asumido” y reclusión segmentada: El nuevo protocolo de Gendarmería para internos trans - La Tercera
sources.claim_summary: La Tercera (in Spanish): Chile's prison service (Gendarmería) signed a new protocol for trans inmates - placement according to gender identity, segmented housing, medical examination on entry to determine hormonal/surgical treatment needs, and respect for assumed-gender expression.

sources.title: Chile - F&M Global Barometers
sources.claim_summary: F&M Global Barometers country profile for Chile: composite scores measuring LGBT rights perception, including a specific Global Barometer of Transgender Rights index.

sources.title: Injusticia en Carabineros: el caso de Isabella Panes, primera policía trans – El Universal Chile
sources.claim_summary: El Universal Chile (April 2025, in Spanish): Isabella Panes, Chile's first trans police officer, sued Carabineros for discrimination - relegated to administrative tasks, private life exposed without consent, denied support against online hate, and transition-related surgery refused.

sources.title: Achievements – Movilh Chile
sources.claim_summary: Movilh (Chilean LGBT integration movement) achievements page: lists the organisation's historical milestones across legal, judicial, public-policy, human-rights, mobilisation and international sectors benefiting lesbians, gays, bisexuals and trans people in Chile - institutional-culture context.
